newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FULL TEXT - BEKAERT EARNINGS STATEMENT.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - BEKAERT EARNINGS STATEMENT.

text.p: Belgian steel wire and cord maker Bekaert released the following statement on 1996 results:
Consolidated profit
Bekaert reports consolidated profit for 1996 of BEF 2,273 million, a 29 % decrease compared to 1995.

The 1996 profit includes two one-off items, a capital gain of BEF 2,306 million on the sale of 10.1 million BMA shares and a provision of BEF 1,929 million net for the structural profit improvement programme announced in December 1996. Excluding these items, consolidated profit for 1996 amounted to BEF 1,895 million, a 40 % decrease compared to the year before.
The decline in the 1996 profit can be attributed mainly to lower sales volumes in Steel Wire and Steel Cord and to increased depreciation.
Sales

Consolidated sales of BEF 61.8 billion were 1.9 % higher than in 1995. A fall in sales volume of 6.7 % in Steel Wire and Steel Cord was compensated by : price increases and improvements in the product mix which had a favourable effect on sales of 3.6 % ; the acquisition of Trifilest and the first full year consolidation of Risler which increased sales by 3.8 % ; a positive impact on sales of 1.2 % for foreign currency movements. Combined sales in 1996 for the consolidated companies and participations amounted to BEF 77.2 billion, an increase of 1 % on a like for like basis.
Sales by business segment
Steel Wire and Steel Wire Products' consolidated sales increased by 2.7 % while volume decreased by 0.7 %.
Steel Cord's consolidated sales decreased by 3.9 %, due to a 5.7 % decline in volume.
Sales of New Activities increased by 15 %.
Profitability

Consolidated operating profit, excluding the provision for the structural profit improvement programme, decreased by BEF 1.1 billion in 1996 due to lower sales volume and higher depreciation. Consequently, profitability of the Group (operating profit as a percentage of sales) decreased from 6.4 % in 1995 to 4.5 % in 1996. Consolidated gross margin (operating profit plus depreciation) as a percentage of sales, and excluding the above mentioned provision, decreased from 12.8 % in 1995 to 11.4 % in 1996.
Cash flow

Consolidated cash flow in 1996 was BEF 8,277 million. Excluding the capital gain on BMA shares, cash flow was BEF 5,971 million compared with BEF 6,183 million in 1995. Despite poor trading conditions the Group was able to maintain cash flow close to the 1995 level.
Capital expenditure
Capital expenditure in the consolidated companies rose to BEF 5.7 billion, up 19 %. This increase is mainly due to the investments in North America and Central Europe.
Total investment by the consolidated companies and participations amounted to BEF 7.7 billion in 1996, compared with BEF 6.1 billion in the prior year, excluding BMA.
Financial position
The Group's financial position remains strong, equity representing 53.4 % of total assets at the end of 1996 compared to 53.6 % at the end of 1995.
Net debt decreased from BEF 8 billion at the end of 1995 to BEF 7.5 billion at the end of 1996.
Higher capital expenditure and lower profit was more than compensated by income from the sale of BMA shares.
NV Bekaert SA (Statutory reporting)
NV Bekaert SA, the parent company, saw its sales decrease by 1.9 %, from BEF 29.1 billion in 1995 to BEF 28.5 billion in 1996.

The 1996 profit was BEF 3,021 million compared to BEF 1,384 million in 1995. The 1996 profit includes a capital gain on the sale of BMA shares of BEF 4,034 million and a provision for the structural profit improvement programme of BEF 1,333 million. Excluding these two one-off items, 1996 profit was BEF 320 million.
Dividend

The Board of Directors will propose to shareholders to maintain the dividend for the 1996 financial year at the level of 1995 and to declare a net dividend of BEF 450 per ordinary share and BEF 510 per share with reduced withholding tax (VVPR).
Outlook

The first months of 1997 have seen better activity at plant level due to improved economic conditions combined with an aggressive market approach. Barring serious unforeseen circumstances, Bekaert expects to make progress towards increased profitability.
